We set up a test where an annotator is provided with a target word in context and a set of substitutes that are equally distributed among the gold and the generated ones. The annotator is required to select, if there are any, all the substitutes that are not suitable replacements for the target in the given context.

guideline: The annotator had to select all the inappropriate substitutes, sticking to the following guidelines: 1. A substitute is wrong if it is an inflection of the target. 2. A substitute is wrong if its replacement modifies the meaning of the sentence. 3. A substitute is wrong if its replacement in the context results in a wrong structure of the sentence. 4. A substitute is wrong if it has an inflected form that is different from that of the target. 5. A substitute is correct if it is in its base form and not in the same inflection as that of the target.

Annotators must select all substitutes that are not suitable replacements; guidelines state a substitute is wrong if it is an inflection of the target, changes the sentence meaning, or results in a syntactically wrong sentence.
